heroData.title: Hire in Poland (No Entity)
heroData.subtitle: EU Tech Hub
heroData.description: Fastest way to hire Polish developers without a local Sp. z o.o. EOR handles ZUS, PIT, and PPK compliance.

steps.title: Medical Examination
steps.description: Mandatory 'Medicine of Labour' (Medycyna Pracy) checkup must be completed before the employee's start date. The employer covers the cost (approx 100-200 PLN) and provides a referral form.

steps.title: BHP Training
steps.description: Occupational Health & Safety (BHP) training is mandatory for all employees. Initial training lasts 1 day and must be refreshed every 3-5 years. This covers office ergonomics and fire safety.

steps.title: Contract Execution
steps.description: Employment contracts must be in Polish or bilingual. Qualified Electronic Signatures (QES) like DocuSign or Autenti are legally valid for employment contracts in Poland.

steps.title: ZUS Registration
steps.description: The EOR partner registers the employee with the Social Insurance Institution (ZUS) using form ZUS ZUA within 7 days of the contract start date.

steps.title: IT & Assets Dispatch
steps.description: If providing hardware, it should arrive 2 days before the start date. PPE or specific work equipment must be documented in a handover protocol signed by the employee.

items.title: B2B Reclassification Risk (2026)
items.text: Starting Jan 2026, the Labor Inspectorate (PIP) will have increased powers to convert B2B contracts into employment contracts instantly if they show signs of subordination (fixed hours, manager oversight). EOR is the safest alternative.

items.title: Notice Period Tenure
items.text: Notice periods are fixed by law: 2 weeks for tenure < 6 months, 1 month for tenure 6 months to 3 years, and 3 months for tenure > 3 years. These cannot be shortened by contract.

items.title: KUP (Creator Tax Costs)
items.text: Poland offers a 50% Tax Deductible Cost (KUP) for employees transferring Intellectual Property. This is highly effective for software developers, increasing Net take-home by up to 10-15%.

items.title: Holiday Allowance
items.text: Employees with < 10 years of seniority (aggregated from education and previous jobs) get 20 days. Those with > 10 years get 26 days. University graduates gain 8 years of seniority automatically.

items.title: Remote Work Regulations
items.text: Under the 2024 Labor Code update, employers must pay a monthly remote work allowance (Ekwiwalent) covering electricity and internet costs, typically 50-100 PLN.

rows.label: Management Fee
values: Per employee, per month management fee.

rows.label: Social Security (ZUS)
values: Employer burden on top of Gross salary.

rows.label: Security Deposit
values: Refundable deposit held until contract termination.

rows.label: Training/Medical
values: One-time setup cost for BHP and medical check.

faqs.question: Can I hire a Polish contractor via EOR?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they are typically converted to a 'Contract of Employment' (UoP) to ensure full compliance. If you need them to stay B2B, the provider acts as a 'Contractor Management' portal rather than EOR.

faqs.question: What is the probation period in Poland?
faqs.answer: The maximum probation period is 3 months. It must be clearly stated in the contract. Termination during probation only requires 1-2 weeks of notice depending on the duration.

faqs.question: Is a 13th-month salary required?
faqs.answer: No. In Poland's private sector, 13th-month salaries are not mandatory. They are common only in public administration and some specific industry unions (like mining).

faqs.question: How do sick leaves work with EOR?
faqs.answer: Employees get paid 80% of their salary during sick leave. The employer (via EOR) pays for the first 33 days per year; after that, the Social Insurance Institution (ZUS) takes over payments.

faqs.question: Does EOR handle the PPK pension?
faqs.answer: Yes. EOR providers must legally auto-enroll employees into the Employee Capital Plans (PPK). Employees can choose to opt-out, but the EOR must manage the deductions and employer contributions of 1.5%.

faqs.question: Can I fire an employee easily with EOR?
faqs.answer: Termination requires a valid reason if the contract is for an 'indefinite' term. EOR providers handle the legal documentation (Wypowiedzenie) and ensure the reason meets Polish Labor Court standards.

items.title: Bilingual Contracts
items.text: Mandatory if the manager is non-Polish. The Polish version remains the source of truth for local courts.

items.title: UODO Data Processing
items.text: EOR must have a signed DPA. Poland has separate laws for monitoring employees (CCTV/E-mail).

items.title: Medical Referrals
items.text: Referral for medical exams must specify all environmental hazards (e.g., computer use >4h, driving).

steps.title: Fixed Data Collection
steps.description: By the 25th of the month, collect timesheets, overtime hours, bonuses, and sick leave certificates (e-ZLA).

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculation
steps.description: Calculations must include ZUS (Pension, Disability, Sickness, Health), PIT advances, and PPK deductions for each employee.

steps.title: Client Approval
steps.description: Payroll register and funding request sent to client. Standard approval deadline is the 28th to ensure timely payment.

steps.title: Salary Disbursement
steps.description: Payments must reach employee accounts by the 10th of the following month, though many companies pay by the last day of the current month.

steps.title: Statutory Reporting
steps.description: Submit ZUS DRA reports by the 15th and PIT-4 tax advances by the 20th of the following month.

items.title: Tax Free Amount (2025)
items.text: The tax-free allowance remains at 30,000 PLN per year. This is applied monthly (250 PLN reduction in tax) unless the employee requests otherwise.

items.title: 32% Tax Threshold
items.text: Once an employee's annual gross exceeds 120,000 PLN, their PIT rate jumps from 12% to 32% on the excess.

items.title: The Zero PIT for Youth
items.text: Employees under 26 years old are exempt from PIT on income up to 85,528 PLN per year. This is a massive hiring incentive.

items.title: PPK Contribution Rates
items.text: Basic: Employer 1.5% + Employee 2.0%. Total 3.5% into private savings.

items.title: L4 Sick Pay
items.text: The first 33 days of illness per year are paid by the employer at 80% of salary.

faqs.question: What is the ZUS deadline?
faqs.answer: The 15th of the following month for entities.

faqs.question: Do I pay tax on benefits?
faqs.answer: Yes, benefits-in-kind (like health insurance or gym cards) are added to gross income and taxed at 12/32%.

faqs.question: What is the annual PIT-11?
faqs.answer: It's the mandatory earnings statement given to employees by end of February for previous year taxes.

items.title: Employer Burden (~20.48%)
items.text: Includes Pension, Disability, Labor Fund, and Accident insurance.

items.title: Employee Deductions (~13.71% + 9%)
items.text: Includes ZUS Social and Health Insurance (Zdrowotna).

steps.title: Gross Base Entry
steps.description: Select monthly or annual gross salary in PLN. Ensure you differentiate between Base and Bonus components.

steps.title: Social Security (ZUS)
steps.description: Automated slicing for Pension (9.76%), Disability (1.5%), and Sickness (2.45%) from the gross amount.

steps.title: Tax Free Deduction
steps.description: Applying the 30,000 PLN annual tax-free threshold (approx 250 PLN monthly tax reduction).

steps.title: PPK Opt-in Modeling
steps.description: Modeling the impact of the 2.0% employee and 1.5% employer contribution to the pension scheme.

steps.title: Final Net Calculation
steps.description: Presentation of 'Take-home pay' after PIT advances and health insurance (Zdrowotna) deductions.

items.title: 12% Entry Bracket
items.text: The standard PIT rate for the first 120,000 PLN of annual taxable income.

items.title: 30-Fold Cap (ZUS Cap)
items.text: Once annual earnings hit approx 234,000 PLN, social insurance (Pension/Disability) contributions stop, increasing net pay for H2.

items.title: Contractor B2B Flat Rate
items.text: For IT contractors, a flat tax rate (Ryczałt) of 8.5% or 12% is often much more efficient than the standard bracket.

items.title: Health Insurance (9%)
items.text: The 9% health insurance contribution is calculated based on (Gross - ZUS Social) and is NOT tax-deductible.

items.title: Student Exemption
items.text: Students under 26 working on a 'Mandate Contract' (Uzlec) enjoy 0% ZUS and 0% PIT in most cases.

items.title: Solidarity Levy
items.text: An additional 4% tax applies to income exceeding 1,000,000 PLN per year.

faqs.question: What is the 'Super-Gross' cost?
faqs.answer: The total cost to the employer, adding approx 20.48% (Employer ZUS) on top of the agreed Gross salary.

faqs.question: How does the Zero PIT for Youth work?
faqs.answer: Employees under 26 pay 0% PIT on income up to 85,528 PLN per year, significantly boosting their net take-home.

faqs.question: What is the tax-deductible cost (KUP)?
faqs.answer: A standard 250 PLN/mo deduction for all, or 50% KUP for creative workers like developers (specific rules apply).

faqs.question: Is PPK mandatory?
faqs.answer: Entry is auto-enrollment, but employees can officially sign an opt-out form every 4 years.

items.title: Node.js & Go Dominance
items.text: Top trending backends in Poland (2025). The local community is heavily invested in distributed systems and microservices architecture.

items.title: Cloud Experts Pool
items.text: Huge AWS/Azure/GCP talent pool due to large engineering hubs for these giants in Warsaw and Wroclaw.

items.title: Talent Retention (1.8y)
items.text: Average tenure in Polish IT is approx 1.8 years. Focus on Developer Experience, modern tech stacks, and remote-first policies to increase loyalty.

items.text: Strong financial sector dominance keeps Java relevant, but Green-field projects are moving rapidly toward Kotlin and Scala.

faqs.question: What is the typical timezone overlap?
faqs.answer: Poland is UTC+1. It offers 100% overlap with Western Europe, 4-6 hours with US East Coast, and early morning sync for US West Coast.

faqs.question: Is IP ownership protected?
faqs.answer: Yes. Polish MSA contracts follow EU-standard IP transfer laws. We ensure 'Economic Copyright' is transferred irrevocably upon payment.

faqs.question: Can I hire developers for on-site relocation?
faqs.answer: While most are remote-first, agencies can support 'Relocation as a Service' (RaaS) for key hires moving to the client's HQ.

faqs.question: How quickly can a team start?
faqs.answer: Standard T&M bench developers can start in 2-4 weeks. Bespoke recruited teams typically require 2-3 months.
